title: Playing opposite Ellington and Armstrong at Roseland
summary: Two bandstands at Roseland, with Armstrong clowning, and daytime recording with night dances.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, I played alongside of Duke Ellington, see? Yeah. At the Roseland Ballroom. They have two bandstands there, see? And they used to have that for a novel. They had one colored orchestra and one white orchestra. And when the Victor band opened up, why... We had a good band. And this Duke Ellington band was good. And also... Do you have one? No, the... Cornette player, Armstrong. Oh. I played alongside of Armstrong, I was saying, see? And Armstrong would come up there. We used to have more fun with Louis than the Mel, see? He'd come up there with a ballet. Come upon a bandstand with his Coon Wright coat on, you know? And have his ballet to take the coat off right where all the people could see him. And he'd stand up there, you know, and throw a lot of murky shines. And he had all the dancers laughing. And he used to stand on the other side too and play against us. We've made several trips to Oakland Ballroom, see? That used to be our stop-and-all-place there. And in the daytime, we'd record. And then at night, we'd play at Ballroom, see? That's... That's what they kept going to Oakland Ballroom. That's what they kept going to Oakland Ballroom. That's what they kept going to Oakland Ballroom. That's what they kept going to Oakland Ballroom.
